Rashi on Shabbat 10a:10:1.english: [People] stand naked - [This is the] inner [room].

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:10:2.hebrew: ערומים ולבושים - אמצעי, שיוצא בו ערום וממהר לכסות את עצמו, ויוצא לחיצון:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:10:2.english: Naked and dressed - [This is the] middle [room], into which one emerges naked and hurries to cover himself, and [then] goes out to the outer [room].

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:11:1.hebrew: וחולץ תפילין - מראשו, ואין צ"ל שאם אוחזן בידו בתיק שלהן שאינו מניח. והא דתני ואין צ"ל כו' — איידי דבעי למיתני מציעתא: ואינו מניח ואינו חולץ; שאמצעי לא כמרחץ גמור הוא, ומקצת תורת מרחץ עליו. הלכך, היו בראשו — אין צריך לחלוץ; היה אוחזן — אסור להניחן שם בראשו, אלא יוצא לחיצון ומניחן:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:11:1.english: And he removes tefillin - From his head. And needless to say, if he is holding them in his hand in their case, he does not don [them]. And that which it teaches, "and needless to say, etc." — [this is] because it needed to teach in the middle [clause], "and he does not don and does not remove." For the middle [room] is not like a full bathhouse, yet part of the halakhic status of a bathhouse applies to it; therefore, [if] they were [already] on his head, he does not need to remove [them]; [if] he was holding them, it is forbidden to don them there on his head; rather, he goes out to the outer [room] and dons them.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:12:1.english: Even though there is no excrement in it - That they cleared it from there.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:13:1.hebrew: בחדתי - שלא רחץ בו אדם מעולם, אלא שהזמינו לכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:13:1.english: In a new [bathhouse] - In which a person has never bathed, but rather he designated it for this [purpose].

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:1:1.hebrew: לא שכיחא שכרות - אין דרך להשתכר מבע"י, לפיכך גומר ויתפלל. אבל בלילה, עשוי להשתכר בסעודתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:1:1.english: Drunkenness is uncommon - It is not usual to get drunk while it is still day; therefore, he may finish [his meal] and [then] pray. But at night, one is likely to get drunk during their meal.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:1:2.english: Prepare to greet your God - Adorn yourself before Him.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:2:1.hebrew: רמי פוזמקי - נותן אנפילאות חשובים ברגליו, ובלע"ז קאלצו"ס:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:2:1.english: Put on socks - He puts fine socks on his feet, and in Old French, *calces* [stockings].

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:2:2.hebrew: שדי גלימא - משליך אדרתו מעליו, שלא יראה כחשוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:2:2.english: Cast off [his] cloak - He casts off his cloak from upon himself, so that he does not appear important.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:2:3.hebrew: ופכר ידיה - חובק ידיו באצבעותיו — מרצי"ר בלע"ז — כאדם המצטער מאימת רבו:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:2:3.english: And clasped his hands - He clasps his hands with his fingers — in Old French, *marcir* [to clasp] — like a person who is distressed from fear of his master.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:3:1.hebrew: חיי עולם - תורה. תפלה צורך חיי שעה היא — לרפואה, לשלום ולמזונות:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:3:1.english: Eternal life - [This refers to] Torah. Prayer is a need of temporal life — for healing, for peace, and for sustenance.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:3:2.english: It grew late - It was late.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:4:1.hebrew: דיינין מתעטפין בטליתן - כשפותחין בדין, מאימת שכינה, ושלא יפנו ראשן לכאן ולכאן, ותהא דעתן מיושבת עליהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:4:1.english: The judges wrap themselves in their cloaks - When they begin judging, [they do so] out of awe of the Divine Presence, and so that they will not turn their heads this way and that, and [so that] their minds will be composed.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:4:2.hebrew: עסיקי ואתו - בדין אחר, וכבר מעוטפים הן. וכשנגמר אותו דין, בא לפניהם דין אחר סמוך למנחה — הויא התחלתן משיפתחו בעלי הדין בטענות, דהכא ליכא למימר משיתעטפו:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:4:2.english: They were already engaged - In another case, and they are already wrapped [in their cloaks]. And when that case concluded, another case came before them close to *minchah* — their beginning is from when the litigants open with [their] claims, for here it cannot be said: "From when they wrap themselves."

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:5:1.english: The pillars - Upon which the upper story of the study hall rested.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:5:2.english: Their hearts grew weak - [They were] distressed that they did not engage in Torah [study] that day.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:5:3.hebrew: תנא להו חייא בר רב - שגדול שכר הדיינים, ולא יצטערו. ול"נ, דאין זה [משמעות] לשון לבייהו, אלא לשון חלש דעתייהו. ולשון חלש לבייהו — לשון תענית הוא, שלא סעדו כל היום. תנא להו חייא בר רב — שאין צריכין לישב ולידון כל היום, אלא מקצת היום. ומה שאמר מן הבקר עד הערב — מדרש הוא, שחשוב הדבר כמעשה בראשית, שנאמר בו ערב ובוקר:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:5:3.english: Ḥiyya bar Rav taught them - [He taught them] that the reward of judges is great, so that they would not be distressed [over missing their Torah study]. But it seems to me that this is not [the meaning of] the phrasing 'their heart [grew weak],' but rather the phrasing 'their mind was weakened' [i.e., they were dejected]. And the phrasing 'their heart grew weak' is an expression of fasting — that they had not eaten all day. [Therefore,] Ḥiyya bar Rav taught them that they do not need to sit and judge all day, but only part of the day. And that which [the verse] says, 'from morning until evening,' is an exposition: that the matter is considered like the Work of Creation, regarding which it is stated: 'evening and morning.'

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:6:1.hebrew: שמלכך - דיינך, שהדיין קרוי מלך, שנאמר: "מלך במשפט יעמיד ארץ" (משלי כ״ט:ד׳):
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:6:1.english: That your king - [This means] your judge, for a judge is called a king, as it is stated: "A king by justice establishes the land" (Proverbs 29:4).

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:7:1.hebrew: לודים - אומה שקורין קנלינ"ש, ואוכלי אדם הן, והם רעבתנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:7:1.english: Ludim - A nation that they call *canilens*, and they are eaters of human [flesh], and they are ravenous.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:7:2.hebrew: מאכל יורשים - יורשי הון רב שלא טרחו בו, ואין עסוקים ודואגין לשוט אחרי מזונות ולעסוק במלאכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:7:2.english: The meal of heirs - [This refers to] heirs to great wealth, who did not toil for it, and are not occupied and worried about roaming in search of sustenance and engaging in labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:8:1.hebrew: כזורק אבן לחמת - קשה לגוף. ולי נראה: לא קשה ולא יפה:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:8:1.english: Like throwing a stone into a waterskin - [It is] harmful to the body. But to me it seems: [It is] neither harmful nor beneficial.

Rashi on Shabbat 10a:9:1.hebrew: מרחצאות שלהן - ג' חדרים היו לו: פנימי — להזיע ולהשתטף; אמצעי — שיורד לתוכו מן המרחץ ולובש חלוקו; ויוצא לחיצון וגומר לבישתו, ונח שם שעה מיגיעת המרחץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 10a:9:1.english: Their bathhouses - It had three rooms: an inner [room] to sweat and rinse off; a middle [room], into which one descends from the bath and puts on his robe; and he goes out to the outer [room] and finishes his dressing, and rests there for a while from the fatigue of the bath.

Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:1:1.hebrew: התם לא שכיחא שכרות - וא"ת: דבריש פ' בתרא דתענית (דף כו: ושם) אמרינן: שחרית ומוסף דכל יומא — לא שכיח שכרות, לא גזרינן; מנחה ונעילה — דשכיח שכרות, חיישינן. אלמא גם במנחה שכיח שכרות! וי"ל: דהתם, לענין נשיאת כפים שאני, דאפילו לא שתה אלא רביעית — אסור לישא את כפיו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:1:1.english: "There, drunkenness is not common" - And if you say that at the beginning of the last chapter of Ta'anit (26b and there) we say: [Regarding] Shacharit and Musaf of every day, drunkenness is not common, [so] we do not decree; [regarding] Mincha and Ne'ilah, where drunkenness is common, we are concerned — evidently, at Mincha, too, drunkenness is common! And one can say that there, with regard to the Priestly Blessing [nesiat kapayim], it is different, for even if he drank only a revi'it [of wine], he is forbidden to raise his hands [in blessing].

Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:1:2.hebrew: טריחותא למיסר המייניה ועוד ליקו הכי וליצלי ומשני משום שנאמר הכון לקראת אלהיך ישראל - ולא חייש לשנויי קושיא קמייתא. מכאן שצריך לאזור חלציו כשמתפלל. ובמחזור ויטרי מפרש, דטעם דבעינן אזור — שלא יהא לבו רואה את הערוה. ודוקא להן, שלא היה להם מכנסים, לכך היו צריכים לאזור בשעת תפלה; אבל לדידן, שיש לנו אבנט של מכנסים, אין אנו צריכין לאזור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:1:2.english: "Is it a burden to tie his belt? And furthermore, let him stand like that and pray!" And [the Gemara] answers: "Because it is stated: 'Prepare to meet your God, Israel'" - And [the Gemara] was not concerned to answer the first objection. From here [we see] that one must gird his loins when he prays. And in Machzor Vitry it is explained that the reason we require a belt is so that his heart does not see the nakedness. And this [applied] specifically to them, who did not have trousers, and therefore they needed to gird [themselves] at the time of prayer; but for us, who have a waistband on our trousers, we do not need to gird [ourselves].

Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:2:1.hebrew: רמי פוזמקי - מכאן יש להוכיח שאין להתפלל יחף, אלא בט' באב ויו"כ:
Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:2:1.english: Put on socks - From here there is proof that one should not pray barefoot, except on Tisha B'Av and Yom Kippur.

Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:5:1.hebrew: אי איכא דאית ליה דינא ליעול - משמע דעדיף דין מתלמוד תורה. והא דאמרי' בפ' בתרא דמ"ק (דף יז.) גבי ההוא דטרקיה זיבורא ושכיב: עיילוהו למערתא דחסידי ולא קבלוהו, למערתא דדייני וקבלוהו — התם בדיינין שאינן מומחין, שפעמים נוטין אחר השוחד:
Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:5:1.english: "If there is anyone who has a legal case, let him enter" - [This] implies that judgment is superior to Torah study. And [as for] that which we say in the last chapter of Moed Katan (17a), regarding that [man] whom a wasp stung and he died: they brought him into the cave of the pious, but it did not accept him; [they brought him into] the cave of the judges, and it accepted him — there, [it refers to] judges who are not experts, who sometimes incline toward bribery.

Tosafot on Shabbat 10a:5:2.english: "A true judgment to its truth" - [This comes] to exclude a fraudulent case.
